turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: Hey, thanks again for working my Saturday morning. So I'll do your Monday, right?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Monday? I think there's a misunderstanding. I don't work on Mondays. We agreed you'd do my Sunday shift, from twelve to six.

turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: Oh! I was sure you said Monday. Sunday is difficult for me. I have a dentist appointment at eleven.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I see. But I really need Sunday, because I have a family lunch at one. What time does your appointment finish?

turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: At about one. I could be here by two.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Then could you work from two to six? I'll do twelve to two and go to the lunch after that. I'll be about an hour late, but that's better than missing it.

turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: Sorry about the confusion. Should we tell the manager?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Yes, let's send her a message now, so she knows who's working when.

turns.speaker: Partner
turns.text: Good idea. So you do Saturday morning and Sunday from twelve to two, and I do Sunday from two to six.
